scope: Post-open audit; original publication texts/abstracts, not raw records or newly identified paired causal contrast. No endpoint covariance recovered. Preserve all ten candidates.

studies.scope: Manipulated robbery rates in 20 natural Ipomopsis populations; several response levels including fluorescent dye and pollen receipt, fruit fraction and seeds per fruit. Seven archived pollen rows and two fruit rows require treatment/endpoint identity recovery. No exact pairing.

Ant-attended vs ant-excluded Asclepias umbels/stems: similar pollinia insertion, significantly fewer pods initiated, mature pod reduction a trend. Different-clone pollen is authors' proposed mechanism, not measured parentage. Archived fruit endpoint could be initiation or mature pod; exact table and denominators unavailable.

studies.scope: 2023 bract removal vs intact, 43 vs 40 marked inflorescences, both deposition and fruit set recorded at flowering end; flower-level link, parent-plant clustering and covariance not available. 2022 hand-pollination experiment separate. Intervention is structural bract removal, not random assignment of robbery alone.

studies.scope: Natural observational robbery; numbered flowers revisited over three years. Deposition n=1182 flowers; fruit n=868, lost plants from weather/animals; 314 fewer flowers, no common-cohort raw analysis. Both endpoints individually nonsignificant. Conditional pollination failure n=161, 32% intact vs 30% robbed, p=.8578; not a demonstrated compensation effect.

studies.scope: Authors tested non-discrimination, relative visitor prevalence and pollen saturation. Already traced 2015 primary/continuous robbery seed treatments in upstream #267; pollen and fruit archive row identities remain unverified. Two focal stage contexts differ.

Chilopsis: honeybees avoid robbed flowers while effective bumblebees do not. Authors report no detected female reproductive loss (fruit and pollen tubes); visit-level deposition and pollen tubes not interchangeable. Archive positive-to-negative contrast needs original endpoint/arm mapping.

Primary-only, primary+secondary, control treatments. Secondary+primary lowers conspecific pollen grains and reproductive output. Fruit success denominator is mature plus aborted fruits, not all initial flowers. Original data workbook 2016_Richman_IpomopsisSecondaryRobbing.xlsx publicly listed at Dryad 10.5061/dryad.tf71f; raw bytes not yet retrieved. Archive IDs 230/231 and 232/233 require arm attribution.

Four-year Glechoma study, male/female carpenter bee robbing differs in tissue damage, including ovules and nectaries. Same species and some same authors as 2007. Treatment-level contrast IDs and overlap unresolved.

Glechoma natural populations and controlled pollination comparisons of Xylocopa and legitimate visitors. Pollination efficiency not automatically same as open cohort fruit set. Treatment pairing unresolved; possible shared system with 2011.

Ipomopsis common garden and group differences in tolerance; male pollen donation tolerance distinguished from female reproduction. Eight archived pollen and eight fruit rows require identity matching; no independent species replication.
